question: Successful orchidopexy completely normalises the risk of testicular malignancy in a previously undescended testis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — false. The increased lifetime risk of testicular cancer persists after orchidopexy; the operation repositions the testis for surveillance, it does not remove the biological risk. Patients need lifelong monthly self-examination.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is false. Orchidopexy does not abolish the elevated malignancy risk inherent to cryptorchidism; it repositions the testis so that the patient and clinician can monitor it. The risk of germ-cell tumour remains elevated throughout life regardless of when repair was performed.
